notes.text: Overall, Express codebase is mature with extensive test coverage. Main concerns: 1) response.js is a god object needing decomposition, 2) router/index.js has complex control flow with sync stack limit, 3) no lockfile for reproducible builds, 4) prototype mutation in app mounting is fragile. The duplication between res.sendFile/res.sendfile is a clear refactoring target. Test files are large but acceptable for integration testing. Security posture appears solid with proper path validation, cookie signing, and URL encoding practices.

findings.title: Oversized response.js god object (1,179 lines)
findings.description: response.js is 1,179 lines handling 20+ distinct responsibilities: status codes, content negotiation, JSON/JSONP, file sending, redirects, cookies, headers, ETags, caching, rendering, and more. This violates single responsibility principle, makes testing harder, and increases cognitive load.
findings.suggestion: Split into focused modules: res-status.js, res-content-negotiation.js, res-file-transfer.js, res-cookies.js, res-headers.js, res-redirects.js, res-rendering.js. Keep a thin facade in response.js that re-exports.
findings.benefit: Improved maintainability, testability, and readability. Easier to audit security-sensitive parts (cookies, file transfer) in isolation.
findings.risk: Medium - large refactor; requires careful preservation of prototype chain and method chaining. Extensive test coverage in test/res.*.js mitigates risk.

findings.title: Complex control flow with sync stack limit in router handle()
findings.description:
The `handle` function uses a `sync` counter (max 100) to prevent synchronous stack overflow, deferring to `setImmediate` when exceeded. This indicates deeply nested synchronous recursion in the routing loop. The function spans ~200 lines with multiple nested conditionals, error handling paths, and state mutations (req.url, req.baseUrl, req.params).

> Validation: cited 140-250 does not contain the snippet — actual lines are 206-261; citation corrected
findings.suggestion: Refactor into smaller methods: `findMatchingLayer`, `processRouteLayer`, `processMiddlewareLayer`, `trimPrefixAndDispatch`. Consider async iteration pattern to eliminate sync counter.
findings.benefit: Reduces cognitive complexity, eliminates arbitrary sync limit, improves debuggability and error stack traces.
findings.risk: Medium - core routing logic; high test coverage in test/app.router.js (1,112 lines) provides safety net.

verification.note: cited 140-250 does not contain the snippet — actual lines are 206-261; citation corrected

findings.title: Mounted app prototype mutation in app.use
findings.description:
When mounting a sub-app, the code temporarily replaces `req` and `res` prototypes with the mounted app's prototypes via `setPrototypeOf`, then restores them after the mounted app handles the request. This mutation is fragile: if the mounted app throws synchronously or calls `next(err)` without the restoration running, the prototypes remain swapped for subsequent middleware. Also, `setPrototypeOf` is slow and de-optimizes V8.

> Validation: cited 180-210 does not contain the snippet — actual lines are 223-246; citation corrected
findings.suggestion: Avoid prototype mutation. Instead, set `req.app = mountedApp` for the duration and restore. Or create a lightweight wrapper that delegates to the correct app without prototype changes.
findings.benefit: Eliminates prototype mutation hazards, improves performance, simplifies mental model.
findings.risk: Medium - mounting is a core feature; must ensure `req.app`, `res.app`, and prototype methods (like `res.render`) work correctly. Test coverage in test/app.mount.js needed.

verification.note: cited 180-210 does not contain the snippet — actual lines are 223-246; citation corrected

findings.title: Duplicated implementation in res.sendFile and res.sendfile
findings.description:
The deprecated `res.sendfile` (lowercase 'f') duplicates ~50 lines of `res.sendFile` implementation instead of delegating to it. Both functions create a file stream with `send()` and pipe via `sendfile()`. The only differences: `res.sendFile` encodes the path with `encodeURI`, validates absolute path/root, and has more JSDoc. This duplication increases maintenance burden and risk of divergence.

> Validation: snippet not present at the cited location (or anywhere in the file) — cited range kept, confidence heavily reduced
findings.suggestion: Refactor `res.sendfile` to call `res.sendFile` internally (with path encoding handled) and keep only the deprecation wrapper. Or make `res.sendFile` call a shared internal implementation.
findings.benefit: Eliminates code duplication, ensures consistent behavior, reduces maintenance surface.
findings.risk: Low - deprecated alias behavior must remain identical; comprehensive tests exist in test/res.sendFile.js

findings.title: Complex async parameter processing with recursive callbacks in process_params
findings.description:
The `process_params` function implements a custom async state machine using mutually recursive `param` and `paramCallback` functions. This pattern is error-prone, hard to debug (stack traces break across callbacks), and difficult to maintain. It handles parameter deduplication, async callbacks, and error propagation manually.

> Validation: snippet not present at the cited location (or anywhere in the file) — cited range kept, confidence heavily reduced
findings.suggestion: Rewrite using Promise/async-await or a lightweight async iterator helper. Each parameter callback returns a promise; process sequentially with `for await` or `reduce`.
findings.benefit: Cleaner stack traces, easier error handling, more readable control flow, modern Node.js patterns.
findings.risk: Medium - parameter processing is core to routing; must preserve exact semantics (deduplication, error 'route' special case, value restoration). Tests in test/app.param.js cover this.
